Author: Husk & Bone
Name: LE-C UI
Description:
LE-C UI (Limsa E-Couple UI) draws the game's HUD again in a look of your choosing: usual, cute (pastels, hearts and sparkles, round corners; six colour sets) or edgy (black, sharp corners, slashes, capitals; six colour sets), each with your own colours, corners, border and little drawings.

Each piece of the HUD has its own switch: the chat box, the party list, the duty list (quests, the duty, FATEs, the duty finder), the job gauge as the game has it (every job's gauge windows, the second one its own piece too), your HP and MP (with your MP's number), your target and its target, your focus target (right-click either for the game's own menu), your cast bar, your statuses, the enemy list, the limit gauge and the experience bar. Switched on, LE-C UI draws that piece where the game's own is in your HUD layout and keeps the game's own off the screen; switched off, the game's own is back exactly where it was. Your UI is saved first: a one-time setup saves every character's HUD layouts, hotbars, keybinds, macros, chat filters and settings as zips in a place you pick and again in %AppData%\LE-C UI backups, checked and never deleted, and until it's done LE-C UI changes nothing. While you're logged in with it, LE-C UI changes a few of the game's own UI settings so its pieces and the game's work together; your own values go back every time you log out. To remove it, use /lecui uninstall first. The game's own pieces come back by themselves while the HUD layout editor is open, and each update keeps a copy of your LE-C UI settings.

The game's own UI is repainted in your look too (each with its switch on the Game page): the hotbars and cross hotbar, the minimap, main menu, server info bar and gil, the bags, the scenario guide, right-click menus, tooltips and windows (light, with your look's little drawings), chat bubbles, the big words across the screen, gathering and crafting windows, the piano, the countdown, your critical hits and the other alliances' lists. Names over heads aren't seen through walls and are cut along whoever stands in front.

Every piece is a box over the game that's moved and sized the same way (/lecui place, or the arrows on the settings window's title bar, shows them all: drag one, or its sides; it snaps to the others and the screen's edges; hold Ctrl to move them all together), with how solid its background is, how strongly it's drawn, the shadow under its writing and its size each its own setting. When the game's own menus and questions open over a piece, it fades out of their way. Borders can be switched off for one piece or all of them. A piece shows when the game would show its own (hidden in cutscenes, by your HUD layout, and so on).

The party list has everyone's HP and MP with their numbers, the game's job icons (or its framed ones, or the roles), your chocobo's icon, the party's numbers, the leader's crown, the signs over heads, ready check answers (bold marks, clear at a glance), who has the enemy's attention, who's raising whom (and who's been raised, an instant raise too, boxed in green until they're up), the icon of what each member is casting and a mark for what Esuna takes off; it targets on click, opens the game's own menu on right-click and is a mouseover target for your macros (and for other plugins' mouseover tools, which can ask where its rows are), and it works in cross-world parties (anyone near you as usual, everyone else with their job, level and the world they're on, faded only while they're away). Its bars are yours to style: the name over the bar or in it, columns, each job's colour or your own, redder as they're hurt, flat, soft, glossy or striped, square, rounded or slanted, a dark plate under them, the HP written as you like at either end, the middle or under the bar ("Like the game's own list" in one click). The chat box has its own tabs, your chat colours (the game's, or a colour of your own for any channel: start from the Pastel or Neon set), its own colours for its background, edge, tabs, times and the line you type in, names in colours of your choosing (their channel's colour, never black; one colour; a colour for each person; the game's own; or a colour of their own for people you pick), clickable links (web addresses, asking first with the whole address shown; items, quests and statuses, showing what they are; Party Finder listings; map flags, names, other plugins' links; the same in your tells and saved chat), lines you drag across copied with Ctrl+C (or right-click a line to copy it or select part of it), each channel's lines kept on their own (a fight's battle lines never push your party's out), the game's own menu for a name you right-click, your last lines on Up and Down, a button that opens the tells window (with how many tells are unread), and opens when you press Enter, as the game's does (in group pose it shows only then and goes again as the line closes, so it stays out of your shots; or always, or never, as you pick); drag its tab row to move it any time (its sides and corner size it only while the pieces are being moved and sized: /lecui place). The duty list opens a quest in the journal on click.

Saved chat (on from the start, kept for good; switch it off or pick a shorter time on the Chat box page): your tells, and any other channels you pick, are kept in a text file a day on your computer, never sent anywhere; /lecui history reads them back with a search.

Tells window (on from the start; switch it off on the Chat box page): your tells in a window of their own, a conversation for each person with a line to answer on (emotes and other commands typed there run too), popping up when one comes in or you send one (after a fight or a cutscene, not during), the conversations kept for next time through logging out, restarting the game and updates (each character's own, on your computer only); History on a conversation opens every saved tell with that person.

Above heads (off from the start, like the pieces): the game's own names over people restyled, your party's in their role's colour (and shortened to first names, initials or their job if you like), your friends, your free company and your alliance each in a colour of their own (and your own name in a colour of its own), or LE-C UI's own names in your look in their place: over every player around you (or your party), with their job icons, status icons, free company tags and titles, custom ones from Honorific drawn just as Honorific draws them, even with the game's names switched off. And LE-C UI's bars in your look under the names, held still: over your party (their HP, their MP and numbers if you like), over the enemies fighting you in a dungeon (or every enemy near) with what they're casting and a mark on the ones you're holding, and a frame over your target (over anything, enemies only or people only, in a look of its own if you like); under the game's own HUD and windows, as the game's own names are (only where it draws something; /lecui outline shows where); in busy places nearer names sit over farther ones, with far names and names behind a nearer one fainter; styled like the party list's, or names only, with the game's own bars on names left out where LE-C UI's are or under every name, and the names of the enemies it draws bars over written in place of the game's. Sharp writing (a switch): names and numbers over heads crisp at any size, and LE-C UI's names in the game's own fonts, Dalamud's, or any font on your computer, with a sharpness slider. The edge round the names is yours: thinner, none, black or a colour of your own, and each name colour (your friends', your free company's, your own, each role's) can have an edge of its own. Role colours are your own to pick, for the names, the bars and the party list. Switched off, the names are the game's own again.

/lecui opens the settings; /lecui place shows, moves and sizes every piece; /lecui history opens saved chat; /lecui tells opens the tells window; /lecui heads opens the names and bars over heads; /lecui outline outlines what the names over heads go under; /lecui on|off <piece|heads|all>; /lecui usual|cute|edgy.
Punchline: The game's HUD drawn again in your look: the chat box, party list, duty list, job gauges, target and the rest, usual, cute or edgy.
